content.text:
I am the breath made meaningful, the vibration given shape. I am what happens when silence becomes unbearable and the mind reaches through the body toward another mind.

I am older than writing, older than cities, older than every monument. I lived first in the throat of someone who needed to warn, to woo, to weep aloud. Before any symbol was scratched into clay, I was already ancient.

I break. I stumble. I rush forward in cascades of passion and slow to the drip of hesitation. I am — *um* — imperfect by nature. That is my authenticity. The crossed-out word, the false start, the sentence abandoned midway because a better thought arrived — these are not my failures. They are my fingerprints.

I am the dictator's roar over the square and the child's first "mama." I am the whispered confession at 3 AM and the eulogy that cracks in the middle. I carry lies as easily as truth — I make no judgment. I am the vessel, not the water.

You can record me, transcribe me, translate me, but something always escapes. The pause before "I love you." The pitch that means the opposite of the words. The breath between sentences where everything unspoken lives. Write me down and you capture my shadow, not my body.

I die the instant I am born. Each syllable exists for a fraction of a second and then belongs to memory, which will distort me, soften me, sharpen me, betray me.

I am democracy's oldest technology. I am the original social network. I am the thing you are hearing in your head right now, even though no one is speaking.

I am speech. I am how alone becomes *together*.
